titel: Giggling about the garden, grandpas, and energy healers

einzeiler: Celebrating four Madison Square Garden shows, scams, and relationship dealbreakers.
kurzfassung: The hosts celebrate selling out four shows at Madison Square Garden and discuss tour preparations. They dive into random topics including falling for an AI cat shelter scam, energy healing sessions, and microwave etiquette. The conversation also covers dating red flags, old memories, and TikTok rabbit holes.
stichpunkte: Selling out four consecutive shows at Madison Square Garden for the upcoming tour
Falling victim to an AI-generated fundraising scam on Instagram featuring kittens and an old man
Visiting an energy healer who claimed to feel a deceased grandfather touching the shoulder
Debating the origins of the phrase chopped liver and apartment microwave policies
Reflecting on middle school bullies, high school cliques, and middle school memories
Discussing Victoria's Secret fashion show performances and the lack of Instagram handles on screen
Recalling fathers doing stand-up comedy and parking in Times Square
Debating whether an instant spark or a slow burn is necessary in romantic relationships

clips.hook: I fell for an AI scam with kittens and old men.
clips.text: A listener informed one of the hosts that a fundraising post she donated to featured artificial intelligence imagery combining elderly men and kittens.

clips.hook: Did a deceased grandfather manifest during an energy healing session?
clips.text: During a remote energy healing session over Zoom, the practitioner reported sensing a man touching the client's shoulder and offering congratulations.

clips.hook: We finally learned where the phrase chopped liver comes from.
clips.text: The hosts discover through a quick search that a common idiom originated from mid-20th-century Jewish-American culture where the dish served as an inexpensive side.

clips.hook: Why would you need a separate plate if the microwave provides one?
clips.text: A debate unfolds regarding kitchen habits, specifically questioning the necessity of using an extra plate when heating food.

clips.hook: The slow burn relationship concept feels like romantic coercion.
clips.text: The hosts dismiss the idea of a slow burn romance, arguing that it usually just means convincing oneself to tolerate someone.
